四人、と数えるべきなのか。誰が男で。誰が女で。誰が、子どもで……。: Should I count them as four people? Who was the man, who was the woman, who were the children...?
そういったものがなんとかわかる程度の輪郭が、ゆらゆら、ぶら下がった裸電球の光に照: Their outlines, just distinct enough to make out those details, flickered and swayed under the light of a dangling bare bulb.
食事中、なのだろうか。: Were they in the middle of a meal?
テーブルに並べられた皿には調理済みの料理が盛りつけられている。: The plates lined up on the table were heaped with cooked food.
人影たちはしきりに箸（を持っているように見える）を伸ばしていた。: The shadowy figures kept reaching out with chopsticks (or at least, they looked like they were holding them).
影たちが何を話しているのか、どんな表情で空間を共にしているのか。: What the shadows were talking about, what sort of expressions they wore as they shared that space...
それでも楽しげな雰囲気だけは見て取れた。: Even so, I could clearly sense the cheerful atmosphere.
いつか遠い時の中、この町であった出来事が[・|繰][・|り][・|返][・|し]: Something that had happened in this town in the distant past was being played back here over, and over, and over again.
そんな幸せだったのだろう誰かの人生を、誰かの瞬間を、覗いていたら……。: Peeking in on someone's life, on someone's moment that must have been so happy...
なぜか俺は、その様子を食い入るように見ていた。: For some reason, I found myself staring transfixed at the scene.
窓はぴったりと閉ざされている。はずなのに――: The window was shut tight. It should have been, and yet--
異様なほど甘い香りに馥郁とされた空気が漏れ出してくる。: Air thick with an unnaturally sweet fragrance came seeping out.
その団欒の中に加わりたい気分にさせられてしまう。: It made me feel like I wanted to join that happy family circle.
[・|こ][・|こ][・|は][・|夜][・|が][・|停][・|滞][・|し]: This was a time where the night had stagnated. Forever. For all eternity.
あの影と同じように自分もなれれば……。: If only I could become just like those shadows...
全部がどうでもよくなった――とまでは言わないし、言えもしないが。: I wouldn't go so far as to say nothing mattered anymore--I couldn't say that, either, but...
ちょっとくらい休んでみてもいいんじゃないかなあ。: Maybe it wouldn't hurt to rest for just a little while.
十夜にきゅっと手を握られ我に返る。: Toya squeezed my hand tightly, snapping me back to my senses.
大雅。あんまり見てたら取り込まれちゃうかも。“迷子”に、なっちゃうかも……。そし: "Taiga. If you stare too long, you might get pulled in. You might become a 'Lost One'... And then you won't be able to come back."
ふるふると首を振り、微笑んで、言った。: I gave my head a little shake, smiled, and spoke.
ミイラ取りがミイラになっちゃ笑い種にもなれないしね: "If the rescuer ends up needing rescuing, it wouldn't even be funny. Like a mummy hunter becoming a mummy."
大雅はすぐ怖いことを言う: "You always say scary things right away, Taiga."
気を取り直し、俺たちはまた進む。: Pulling ourselves together, we pressed on once more.
一軒の古民家の前を通る。: We passed in front of an old traditional house.
また、ちょうど明かりが灯った。: Just then, another light came on.
木枠の格子がはめ込まれた窓から淡い光が漏れている。: A pale glow leaked through a window fitted with a wooden lattice.
歩きながら……まただ。: As I walked... there I went again.
ふと、窓から中を見てしまう。: Without thinking, I found myself peeking inside through the window.
微かな音楽が耳に付き、気になってしまったのだ。: A faint melody had caught my ear, piquing my curiosity.
そこは民家ではなくお店のようだった。: It seemed to be a shop rather than a private home.
楽器屋だろうか。蝶ネクタイと背広できちんと正装をした初老の男性がチェロを弾いてい: A music store, perhaps? An elderly man dressed neatly in a suit and bow tie was playing the cello.
今度は影ではなく人間で……。: This time, it wasn't a shadow, but a human...
身体中から響かせる旋律に[まぶた|瞼]を閉じて――たおやかに。: With his eyelids closed, giving himself over to the melody resonating through his entire body--gracefully.
……重厚な音色の弦楽器ただひとつ。: Just a single stringed instrument with a rich, deep tone.
奏でる旋律は、きっと遙か昔にさみしい誰かが、愛する誰かを想い作られたもの。: The melody he played must have been composed long, long ago by someone lonely, thinking of someone they loved.
ふと、男の隣に女の人の姿が見えた。: Suddenly, I noticed the figure of a woman beside the man.
チェロを弾く男性に、そっと寄り添い――: Gently nestling close to the man playing the cello--
それは壁に飾られた写真の中で微笑む人とよく似た顔をしていた。: Her face looked remarkably like the person smiling in a photograph framed on the wall.
この男性は“迷子”でなければ“影”でもない。ましてや“[・|悪][・|夢]”とも: This man was neither a "Lost One" nor a "shadow." And he certainly wasn't a "Nightmare," either.
[・|心][・|の][・|中][・|で]、[・|夢][・|の][・|中][・|で: He was someone who had come to meet a person precious to him, within his heart, within a dream.
太陽が目覚めれば自然と真昼の世界へ戻るだろう。: Once the sun woke, he would surely return naturally to the midday world.
停滞した夜の刻が終わり始めてる。: The stagnant hour of the night is beginning to end.
“[・|夜][・|の][・|国]”[・|が]、[・|は][・|じ][・|ま][・: The "Country of the Night" is about to begin.
[・|そ][・|の][・|前][・|に][・|舞][・|台][・|を][・|掃]: Our job is to clean the stage before that happens.
灯る明かりが増えていく。: More and more lights were coming on.
あの家も、この家も。: In that house, and this one, too.
そこにある光景はそれぞれ違っていようとも……。: Even if the scenes inside were all different from one another...
おそらく、誰かにとって何より理想的な風景が映し出されているに違いなかった。: Surely, each one was projecting the most ideal scenery imaginable for someone.
十夜が小さな声を上げる。そして道の先を指さす。: Toya let out a small gasp and pointed down the road.
……見つけた。ほら、あそこ。“悪夢”のかけら: "...Found one. Look, over there. A fragment of a 'Nightmare.'"
目をこらし、見る。: I strained my eyes and looked.
闇の中で何かがゆらゆらうごめいていた。: Something was wriggling and swaying in the darkness.
更に見つめると、それは[・|魚]だとわかった。: Staring closer, I realized it was a fish.
ふよふよと夜気を泳ぐように浮かぶ……真っ赤な金魚だ。: Floating weightlessly as if swimming through the night air... a bright red goldfish.
口をぱくぱくとさせながら、[・|そ][・|れ]は、チェロの音色が響く楽器屋のほう: With its mouth opening and closing, it drifted toward the music store where the sound of the cello echoed...
家の明かりに吸い寄せられてる。急いで回収しないと……: "It's being drawn to the light of the house. We have to hurry and collect it..."
灯る明かりの中で[・|彼][・|ら]は夢を見ている。できるだけ幸せな夢を。: Within the glowing lights, they are dreaming. Dreaming the happiest dreams they possibly can.
その幸せな時間に悪い夢が滑り込んでしまわぬよう――さあ、急ごう。: To make sure no bad dreams slip into that happy time--come on, let's hurry.
……もうひとつの“夜”の扉が開くその前に。: Before the door to the other "Night" opens.
今夜も、できるだけたくさんの悪い夢を探して掃除、しなければ。: Tonight, too, we have to find and clean up as many bad dreams as we can.
――“悪夢”のかけらは今夜もたくさんたくさん、見つかった。: --We found lots and lots of "Nightmare" fragments again tonight.
その姿は様々だ。: They came in all sorts of shapes and sizes.
ふよふよ夜気に浮かんだ金魚。真っ赤だったり。真っ黒だったり。白色だったり。金色だ: Goldfish floating weightlessly in the night air. Some were bright red. Some were pitch black. Some were white. Some were golden.
辺りを飛び交う蛍の光――のように見え。: Things that looked like the light of fireflies flitting about the area.
蛍光色のような淡い光の中を良くよく見れば……小さな髑髏が不気味な笑顔を浮かべる“: If you looked closely inside their pale, fluorescent glow... there was "something" like a tiny skull wearing an eerie smile.
……その光りに触れると真っ赤な血が辺りに散らばる。: Touching that light would scatter bright red blood all over the place.
壁や道路の中を泳いで逃げる、影絵のような魚群やイルカたち。: Schools of shadow-puppet fish and dolphins swimming away through the walls and roads to escape.
それらを、一つひとつ適切な方法で捕獲回収していって――: We captured and collected them one by one using the proper methods for each--
十夜がリュックに詰めて持ってきていた、鋼鉄製の鳥かごのような小さな檻に閉じ込めて: And locked them away inside small cages like steel birdcages that Toya had packed into her backpack.
……よく、そんなのリュックサックに入ったね: "...I'm amazed you managed to fit something like that into your backpack."
鳥かごは十夜が両手で抱えなければならない程の大きさだった。: The birdcage was so big that Toya had to hold it with both hands.
このリュックはね、魔法なんだよ。口に通る大きさのものなら何でも入るし、リュックは: "This backpack is magic, you know. Anything small enough to fit through the opening can go inside, and it never, ever gets full."
言いながら、十夜はたった今捕まえた“[金魚|悪夢]”を閉じ込めた鳥かごを、ぐいぐ: As she spoke, Toya shoved the birdcage holding the "Nightmare" goldfish we'd just caught deep into her backpack.
そしてまた新しい鳥かごを取り出す。: Then, she pulled out a fresh birdcage.
それを使って俺はまた一匹金魚を捕まえる。: Using that, I caught another goldfish.
重くない？ そのリュック。いつまでも満杯にならないとはいっても……。重量はないの: "Isn't that backpack heavy? Even if it never gets full... doesn't it still have weight? Though I know you said it's magic."
やっぱり俺がリュックを持つよと言うけれど、十夜はふるふると首を振る。: I offered to carry the backpack for her after all, but Toya shook her head.
これってお姉ちゃんの新しい“[魔法|アイテム]”なんだからと十夜は得意げ。: Toya looked proud, saying that this was her big sister's new magic "item."
どんなにたくさん荷物を詰め込んでも、重さは三分の一なんだってお姉ちゃん言ってた。: "Big Sis said that no matter how much stuff you pack into it, the weight is only one-third. So it's super light."
ううん。もっともっと、軽くなるんだったかも、と十夜は小さな首をかしげていた。: "Wait, no. Maybe it gets even lighter than that," Toya added, tilting her small head.
そうか。“夜の魔法使い”が作った道具だね: "I see. A tool made by the 'Magician of the Night,' huh?"
全然重くないし、軽いんだけどね……: "It's not heavy at all, and it's really light, but..."
十夜は俺を見上げ、目をパチパチとさせながら言った。: Toya looked up at me, blinking her eyes rapidly as she spoke.
帰ったら算数のお時間だな十夜ちゃん: "Looks like it's time for a math lesson when we get back, Toya-chan."
かわいい顔をぎゅ～っとしかめて、十夜は言った。: Scrunching up her cute face tightly, Toya spoke.
大雅なんて嫌いだよ。算数とおんなじくらい大嫌い: "I hate you, Taiga. I hate you just as much as I hate math."
ふわふわ泳ぐ金魚には虫取り網を。: For the goldfish swimming weightlessly through the air, we used a bug net.
血しぶきと小さな髑髏の光は、直接触れないよう、専用の分厚い布で作られた手袋をして: For the blood-splattering lights with tiny skulls, we put on special gloves made of thick cloth so we wouldn't touch them directly, cupping them in both hands.
壁や道路を泳ぐイルカの群れには頑丈な投げ網を使った。: For the pods of dolphins swimming through the walls and roads, we used a sturdy casting net.
投げた網は、まるで海面を沈むみたいに、地面の中に落ちていく。: The cast net sank right into the ground, as if submerging beneath the surface of the sea.
……編み目にかからぬ小さな魚の影たちは、特別製の釣り竿の糸を道路にたらして釣り上: As for the small shadow-fish that slipped through the mesh, we dropped the line of a specially made fishing rod into the road to reel them in.
糸を垂らすと固い道路にぽちゃりと波紋が広がって――: Dropping the line sent a ripple spreading across the hard road with a plop--
腰を下ろした道路のしたを、警戒心をあらわに泳ぎ回る魚群がさーっと素早く通り過ぎて: Right beneath the road where we sat, a school of fish swam past with a swift swoosh, their wariness on full display.
辺りが真っ暗闇に覆われた。: The area was plunged into pitch darkness.
月明かりや星明かりが頭上の[・|何][・|か]に閉ざされる。: The moonlight and starlight were blocked out by something overhead.
するとそこには巨大な魚影が。: There, we saw the colossal silhouette of a fish.
俺たちの頭上を静かに静かに、泳いでいった。: It swam quietly, ever so quietly, right over our heads.
そして、その大きさにぞっともした。: And its sheer size sent a chill down my spine.
そうか。夜空を漂う巨大なくじら、か。: I see. A giant whale drifting through the night sky, huh.
その姿を見上げるこの俺は。: Looking up at its form, I...
否応なく、色々と思い出してしまうのだけれど……。: couldn't help being reminded of all sorts of things...
あんな大きなのがもしも空から降ってきたら、俺たち潰されちゃうのかな。: If something that huge fell from the sky, I wonder if we'd get squashed flat.
そうならなくてよかったねと言ってふたりで笑った――: Saying we were glad that didn't happen, the two of us laughed together--
引き続き一つひとつ時間をかけて、回収できるサイズの“悪夢”を鳥かごに閉じ込めてい: We continued taking our time, locking up the "Nightmares" that were small enough to collect into birdcages one by one.
“悪夢”のかけらに直接触れてしまうと心が危ない。: Touching a fragment of a "Nightmare" directly is dangerous for the heart.
……心が障られ“迷子”になってしまうかも。: It might corrupt your heart and turn you into a "Lost Child."
だから色々な道具を使い――できるだけ多くの“悪夢”のかけらを捕まえる。: That's why we use various tools--to catch as many "Nightmare" fragments as possible.
暖かな明かりの灯る窓がまた増えて――: More windows lit with warm light appeared--
その中で穏やかな夢を見ている誰かの心に、するりと、“悪夢”が逃げ込んでしまわぬよ: and we worked so that no "Nightmare" could slip into the hearts of the people dreaming peacefully inside.
結構たくさん捕まえたね。空いてる籠もなくなっちゃったし、今夜はもういいんじゃない: "We caught quite a lot, didn't we? We're out of empty cages too, so maybe we can call it a night."
最後の金魚を捕まえた鳥かごを、十夜はぐいぐいとリュックに押し込めていた。: Toya was shoving the birdcage holding the last goldfish deep into her backpack.
大雅が一緒だったから今夜はあんまり怖くなかったし……、回収、早く終わったよ: "Since you were with me tonight, Taiga, it wasn't very scary... and we finished collecting them really fast."
ちょっとは役に立てたかな: "Think I managed to be a little useful?"
両腕を大きく開いて見せてくれ、: She spread both arms wide to show me.
すんごい便利な男の子だったよ大雅: "You were a super convenient boy, Taiga."
……むむ。褒められてるのはわかるんだけど素直に喜んで良いのかどうか微妙な気持ちに: "...Hmm. I know I'm being praised, but I have mixed feelings about whether I should just be happy about that."
帰宅の準備を整える。: We got ready to head home.
釣り竿や網だとか、“悪夢”を捕まえるために使った道具を、十夜のリュックに俺も詰め: I helped pack the fishing rod, nets, and other tools we used to catch the "Nightmares" into Toya's backpack.
遠いどこかからクジラの鳴く声がして、俺は夜空をふっと見上げた……。: Hearing a whale's cry from somewhere far away, I glanced up at the night sky...
明らかに“何か”を恐怖している表情だ。: It was the expression of someone clearly terrified of "something."
まさか、という予感が俺の中を足早に駆けていく。: A sudden foreboding raced through me.
十夜のその返答に“やっぱりか”という思いで俺は眉を寄せた。: At Toya's reply, I furrowed my brow, thinking, "Just as I thought."
小さな鼻先をひくひくとさせながら、十夜は夜の闇に呑まれた道の先を指さした。: Twitching the tip of her tiny nose, Toya pointed down the road swallowed by the darkness of night.
この、ずっとずっと先のほうから気配がするよ: "I can sense a presence coming from way, way up ahead."
俺は十夜が指さす先を見る。: I looked in the direction Toya was pointing.
目を細め、立ちこめる闇色の向こうを見透かそうとする。: Narrowing my eyes, I tried to peer through the thick darkness.
嫌な予感がした。: I had a bad feeling about this.
……俺の足は自然と十夜が指さした先へと向かおうとする。: My feet naturally started to move toward where Toya had pointed.
十夜が立ち止まったままだった。: Toya was still standing frozen in place.
手を繋いでいた俺も先へは行けず、足を止めた。: Since we were holding hands, I couldn't go any further either, and stopped in my tracks.
じっと足先に視線を落としたまま、十夜は何も話さない。: Keeping her gaze fixed firmly on her feet, Toya didn't say a word.
どうしたのだろう。どこか調子でも悪いのだろうか。: What was wrong? Was she feeling unwell?
うつむいたままぽつりと十夜が言った。: Still looking down, Toya murmured quietly.
大雅……。この道の先、本当に行くの？ なんだか嫌な予感がする。だからね、もう一回: "Taiga... Are we really going down this road? I have a bad feeling about it. So, promise me one more time."
十夜は小指を立てて見せていた。: Toya held up her pinky finger.
ああ、無茶はしない。約束だ: "Yeah, I won't do anything reckless. I promise."
心配そうにしてくれる十夜へと。: At Toya, who was looking so worried for me.
そして俺も小指を立てて見せた。: And I held up my pinky finger too.
そうだな。“約束”していたもんな。: That's right. We made a "promise," after all.
“どんなことがあっても無茶はしない”“できるだけ無傷で帰ってくる”: "Never do anything reckless no matter what happens," and "Come back as unharmed as possible."
十夜が一緒だから、きっと大丈夫だよ。無事に帰れる: "Since you're with me, Toya, I'm sure it'll be fine. We'll make it back safely."
だから心配しないでと俺は言った。: So don't worry, I told her.
でも。……でもね、私、お姉ちゃんみたいに頼りにならないし: "But. ...But I'm not as reliable as Big Sis."
そんなことはない。十夜は頼りになるし、実際、頼りにしてる: "That's not true. You are reliable, Toya, and I really do count on you."
今夜はここまででいいよ。もう、帰ろう。……今までは怪我だけですんだけど。もしかし: "We've done enough for tonight. Let's just go home. ...Up until now, you've gotten away with just injuries. Maybe we were just lucky."
大雅が痛いのになっちゃったら、私……嫌だよ: "If you end up getting hurt, Taiga, I... I'd hate it."
大丈夫。これまで運がよかったのなら、きっとこれからだって運がいい。だからなんだっ: "It'll be okay. If we've been lucky up until now, I'm sure we'll keep being lucky from here on out. So we can handle anything."
なに言ってるんだこいつ、といった顔だった。: She gave me a look that said, "What is this guy talking about?"
視線の色は非難囂々。ちゃんと危険を理解しているのかと。: Her eyes were full of reproach, asking if I truly understood the danger.
そんな顔もかわいい子だな、などと場違いもいいところなことを思いながら俺は言う。: Thinking completely out-of-place thoughts about how cute she looked even making that face, I spoke up.
いいことを教えようか、十夜。人間はな、誰だって、本当はすごく強いんだぞ。君らが思: "Let me tell you something good, Toya. Humans, no matter who they are, are actually really strong. Much, much stronger than you guys think. That's why we can do anything, no matter what it takes."
十夜は少し黙ってしまう。: Toya fell silent for a moment.
……わかってるもん。知ってるよ。人間は……大雅は、強いよ。でも: "...I know that. I know. Humans are... You're strong, Taiga. But..."
……でもね、大雅。大雅が強いことは知ってるけれど。……昔みたいに、千和や姫織にも: "...But you know, Taiga. I know that you're strong. ...Still, I think if Chiwa and Himeori helped out like they used to, we could be even stronger, don't you?"
そしたら大雅だけが痛い思いするのも、少なくなるかもだよ……: "Then maybe you wouldn't have to be the only one getting hurt so much, Taiga..."
消え入りそうに細くなっていく十夜の声だ。: Toya's voice trailed off, growing faint as if about to vanish.
その言葉を俺、奏大雅はあらゆる意味で嫌悪するのだが――今は、いい。: I, Kanade Taiga, despise those words in every sense--but for now, it doesn't matter.
それについては、僅かにでも懊悩すべき問題では今はまだない。: Right now is not the time to agonize over that, even a little.
十夜。“迷子”のいる場所はどこら辺かな。まだ、遠い？: "Toya. Whereabouts is this 'Lost Child'? Is it still far?"
自分に都合が悪くなりそうな会話を強引にねじ曲げた。: I forcefully steered the conversation away from a topic that was getting inconvenient for me.
十夜は少し戸惑いながらも、かわいい鼻先をひくひくとさせ、: Looking slightly bewildered, Toya twitched the tip of her cute nose.
その、角を曲がったところ。そこから匂いがする: "Just around that corner. The scent is coming from there."
懐中電灯の光で夜を切り取る。: The beam of my flashlight carved through the night.
もうひとつの“夜”がはじまる直前の時間帯。: The time right before the other "Night" begins.
繋いだ小さな手に引かれるままに……ふたりで、進む。: Led along by the small hand holding mine... the two of us moved forward.
十夜いわくこの辺りから“迷子”の気配がするらしい。: According to Toya, the presence of the "Lost Child" was coming from somewhere around here.
そこは通学に利用しているバス停付近。: It was near the bus stop I used to commute to school.

宙を浮かぶように泳ぐ魚が、ぎょろりとした目でこちらを睨んだ――ような気がした。: Swimming as if floating in midair, the fish glared at me with bulging eyes--or so it felt.
まっしろな魚はこぽりとひとつ、気泡を吐き出し逃げていく。: The pure white fish let out a single bloop of a bubble and fled.
まるでリュウグウノツカイのように大きく長い身体をした魚が背後から現れ、俺のすぐ横: A fish with a large, long body just like an oarfish appeared from behind me, swam right past my side, and vanished into the pitch-black darkness.
よく見ればあちこちに魚がゆらりゆらゆらと泳いでいた。: Looking closely, fish were swimming lazily here and there all around me.
ここはまるで、深く冷たい深海のようだった。: This place was just like the deep, freezing ocean floor.
小さな魚の群が、ざざざざざーっと猛スピードで俺を包み、通り過ぎていった。: A school of small fish swarmed around me at breakneck speed with a rushing whoosh and passed right on by.
どうやら大きな魚から逃げていく途中だったらしい。: Apparently, they were in the middle of fleeing from a larger fish.
[・|そ][・|れ][・|ら]はかけらだ。夢のかけら。: Those are fragments. Fragments of dreams.
昨晩、俺と十夜が“夜”の中を回収して歩いたのと、同じもの。: The exact same things Toya and I walked around collecting in the "Night" last night.
……放置しておけばいつしかそれは“悪夢”となって、眠りについた誰かの“心”に滑り: If left alone, they will eventually turn into "Nightmares" and slip into the "heart" of someone who has fallen asleep.
定期的に掃除しなければ、これらは際限などないかのようにどんどん増える。: If we don't clean them up regularly, they will multiply endlessly, as if they know no bounds.
そうしていつか“夜”の世界はパンクする。: And then someday, the world of "Night" will burst at the seams.
すると、人々は“悪夢”ばかりを見るようになってしまう。: When that happens, people will end up having nothing but "Nightmares."
……ここも、十夜と一緒に掃除しにこなけりゃいけないかな: "...Maybe I'll have to come clean up around here with Toya, too."
また少し歩く。石段を登る。: I walk a little further and climb the stone steps.
真ん中辺りまで登ったところで、目の前に糸のようなものが垂れているのに気づいた。: About halfway up, I noticed something like a thread dangling right in front of my eyes.
遙か上空からすらーっと長く。: It stretched straight down in a long line from far up in the sky.
良く見てみると糸の先には釣り針が結ばれていた。その針につけられている餌は……なん: Looking closely, a fishhook was tied to the end of the line. And the bait attached to the hook was... what is that? A tiny light.
その光に吸い寄せられた魚が食らいつく。: Drawn in by that light, a fish snapped at it.
すると、魚はそのまま空高く引き上げられていった。: Immediately, the fish was reeled straight up high into the sky.
懐中電灯の光を、見上げた夜空に向けてみた。: I looked up and pointed the beam of my flashlight toward the night sky.
光の柱が真夜中に吸い込まれていく――: The pillar of light was sucked into the dead of night--
満点の星空が、ゆらゆら、ばしゃばしゃと、揺れていた。: The sky full of stars was swaying and splashing about.
まるで釣り上げた魚が暴れ、水面に波紋が広がるみたいに。: Just like ripples spreading across the water's surface from a hooked fish thrashing around.
きらきら光るあの空は、深い海の底から見上げる海面のようだった。: That sparkling sky looked just like the surface of the ocean seen from the deep sea floor.
また釣り糸がするりと垂れてきた。: Another fishing line dropped smoothly down.
その針先にはほんわりと淡い光を放つ星が付けられていた。: Attached to the tip of its hook was a star giving off a soft, faint glow.
飴玉だ。甘いあまい味の飴玉を餌に“悪夢の魚”を釣り上げる。: A piece of hard candy. Reeling in "Nightmare fish" using sweet, sugary candy as bait.
よく見るとそれはひとつではない。: Looking closely, there wasn't just one.
辺りにいくつも糸が落とされていた。: Numerous lines had been dropped all around the area.
もしあの星に触れ、間違って釣り上げられたらどこへ行くのだろう。: If I touched one of those stars and got reeled up by mistake, where would I end up?
俺や十夜みたいな“悪夢”の回収者が小さなボートに乗って、月明かりに照らされながら: Maybe "Nightmare" collectors like Toya and me are riding in a little boat, fishing under the moonlight.
夜空から垂らされた糸を避けながら、更に石段を登っていく。: Dodging the lines dangling from the night sky, I climb further up the stone steps.
階段を登り切った。すると広がる境内の光景。: I reached the top of the stairs. Before me spread the view of the shrine grounds.
そこもやはり“夜”の中。いつもの風景とは違ってしまっていた。: Naturally, this place was inside the "Night" as well. It had changed from its usual scenery.
ぼんぼりに灯された淡い光は“夜”の闇を照らし出し……[ＳＬ|機関車]だ。: The faint light lit within the paper lanterns illuminated the darkness of the "Night" to reveal... a steam locomotive.
その先頭車両と客室車両がひとつずつ、連結されたものが境内には停められていた。: Parked on the shrine grounds were its lead engine and a single passenger car coupled together.
いつもなら市電の客車部分を社務所に改装したものが置かれている場所にそれはある。: It sat in the spot normally occupied by a streetcar passenger cabin that had been remodeled into the shrine office.
客室車両にも明かりはなく、人の気配はなかったが……。: There were no lights on in the passenger car either, and no sign of anyone inside, but...
……車両の屋根の上。: Up on the roof of the train car.
見上げた屋根に女の子が、ひとり。: Looking up, there was a single girl on the roof.
足をぶらぶらさせるような格好で、座っていた。: She was sitting there, dangling her legs over the edge.
光はそんな女の子の隣に置かれたランタンだった。: The light came from a lantern placed next to her.
大きめの車掌服と、その帽子。: An oversized conductor's uniform, and a matching hat.
そして伸び放題の長い髪を三つ編みに結い――: With her long, overgrown hair tied into braids--
客車の屋根に腰を下ろし、空をじっと見上げていた。: She sat on the roof of the passenger car, gazing fixedly up at the sky.
こんなところで、何やってるのかな: "What are you doing in a place like this?"
また、問いかける。: I call out to her again.
そんなところにいたら風邪ひいちゃうかもしれないよ。でも、まあ、君が風邪とか引くの: "You might catch a cold if you stay up there. Well, though I don't really know if you can even catch a cold or not."
少女は何も答えず夜空を見ていた。: The girl didn't answer at all, just watching the night sky.
俺もつられて空を見上げてみる。: Following her lead, I look up at the sky too.
大きなおおきな満月が、さみしく冷たい“夜”の時間をオレンジ色に照らし出す。: A huge, massive full moon illuminates the lonely, freezing time of "Night" in an orange glow.
ぼんやりと見知らぬ夜空を見上げながらそう思っていた。: I wondered to myself, blankly gazing up at the unfamiliar night sky.
少女のつぶやきが、沈黙に小さな穴を開けたのだ。: The girl's murmur poked a tiny hole in the silence.
だから俺も、夜空を見上げたままそっと返した。: So, still looking up at the night sky, I gently replied.
少女は人差し指を星空に向けた。: The girl pointed her index finger at the starry sky.
今度は誰を、どの星に連れて行かなきゃならないのか……。想像してみてた: "Who I'll have to take next, and to which star... I was trying to imagine it."
奏大雅。あなたが、わざわざここに来るってことは……[・|そ][・|う][・|い]: "Kanade Taiga. For you to come all the way out here... that's what it means, right?"
さすがは“夜”の[・|神][・|さ][・|ま][・|だ]。何でも全部お見通しなん: "Just what I'd expect from the God of the 'Night.' You see right through everything, don't you? I can't keep any secrets from you."
神さまなんかじゃない。と小さな女の子は言う。: I'm no god, the little girl says.
自分が何者なのか知りたいだけの、ただ、ここにいるだけの、“何か”でしかない: "I'm nothing more than a 'something' that is simply here, only wanting to know what I am."
嫌だやめてといわれることを意地悪く続けるのも、それはもちろん、本意ではないけれど: Of course, it's not my intention to be mean and keep doing something she tells me she hates and wants me to stop, but...
どうしてもだめかな、ナナちゃん。君のこと神さまって呼ぶと、なんでだか安心するって: "Can I really not, Nana-chan? When I call you God, how should I put it, it somehow makes me feel relieved..."
女の子は目を細め、屋根の上から俺を見下ろす。: The girl narrows her eyes and looks down at me from atop the roof.
その、ナナちゃんというのもやめてほしい。神さまと呼ばれるのと同じくらい……いや: "Um, I want you to stop calling me Nana-chan, too. Just as much as being called God... I hate it."
いやだから、いや。[・|安][・|直]すぎるから: "Because I hate it, that's why. It's way too simplistic."
そうかな。かわいいって思うけどなあ、俺: "You think so? I think it's cute, though."
……のかと思えば、違った。それは憤怒の表情だった。: Or so I thought, but I was wrong. It was an expression of sheer fury.
……あなたの周りの女の子、みんな、私を“かわいい”と言っておもちゃにする。もみく: "...All the girls around you call me 'cute' and treat me like a toy. They Rumple and squish me. It's traumatic."
……まだまだ俺たちが小さかった頃のこと。: That was back when we were all still very young.
俺たちはよくここへ遊びに来ていた。あるいはナナちゃんの力を借りるため、度々ここへ: We used to come here to play a lot. Or rather, we visited here frequently to borrow Nana-chan's power.
“夜”の魔法使いの“ゆめのねどこ”が、もし俺たちの学校のようなものだとすれば……: If the "Dream Bed" of the Magician of the "Night" was something like a school to us...
ここはまるで託児所のようだった。: Then this place was just like a daycare.
ナナちゃんは当時の俺たちよりもちっこくて。: Back then, Nana-chan was even tinier than we were.
挙げ句、望まぬあだ名まで付けられて――ちっこくてかわいいからとされたい放題されて: And to top it all off, even being given an unwanted nickname--because she was tiny and cute, everyone did whatever they wanted with her.
それこそまるで“ぬいぐるみ”のような扱いだったのだ。: She really was treated just like a stuffed animal.
それも、これも……。: All of this, and all of that...
みんな、みんな。あなたが、奏大雅が、私を“ナナちゃん”だとか呼ぶようになったから: "Every single bit of it. It's because you, Kanade Taiga, started calling me 'Nana-chan.' ...'Nana-chan,' what is that supposed to be? I don't even need a name. It's humiliating."
ナナちゃんはぎりぎりと歯ぎしりするようにしていた。: Nana-chan looked like she was grinding her teeth in frustration.
その様子とかわいい顔が、なんだかとても相反していて……むしろ楽しい。: Her behavior and her cute face contrasted so much that... it was actually kind of amusing.
……大雅。今日はあなた以外には誰も来ていないよね: "...Taiga. Nobody else came with you today, right?"
まだ安心できないのか、きょろきょろとし続けていた。: Still not completely reassured, she kept glancing around restlessly.
抱きしめられるのも頬ずりされるのも……乱暴に振り回されてもみくちゃにされるのも、: "Getting hugged, having my cheeks nuzzled... being swung around roughly and rumpled up, I've had enough of it all. It makes me want to cry."
大丈夫だよ。みんな子どもじゃないから、もうそんなことはないって思うけどな: "You'll be fine. None of us are little kids anymore, so I don't think that'll happen again."
ぷいっとそっぽを向いた。: She turned her head away in a huff.
……いいから。さっさと用事を済ませてしまおう。私は眠いの。すごく眠い: "...Whatever. Let's just get your business over with quickly. I'm sleepy. Very sleepy."
そうして帽子を目深に被った女の子……。: And so, this girl with her hat pulled down low over her eyes...
出会った当初、何者でもない私には名前がないと言っていたそんな彼女に、確かに俺が、: When we first met, she told me that since she was nobody, she had no name. And it's true that I was the one who gave her that name.
彼女の住処であり相棒でもあるこのＳＬに振られた番号が七番だからだ。: That's because the number assigned to this steam locomotive, which is both her home and her partner, is number seven.
確かにそうだ。ナナちゃんの言うとおりあまりに安直だけど……。: It certainly is true. Just as Nana-chan says, it's way too simplistic, but...
幼い頃からずっとそう呼び続けている。故に。もう彼女のことを、“ナナちゃん”か“神: I've been calling her that ever since I was little. Because of that, calling her by any name other than "Nana-chan" or "God" now would just feel completely unnatural.
そんな彼女は――ナナちゃんは、ナナちゃん自身が言うとおり、何者でもないのだろう。: She--Nana-chan, just as she says herself, is probably nobody at all.
人間ではない。動物ではない。植物ではない。むろん、鉱物ではあり得ない。: She isn't human. She isn't an animal. She isn't a plant. And of course, she couldn't possibly be a mineral.
そんな彼女は――いつ、どこで、何のために産まれたのか……。: When, where, and for what purpose was she born...?
彼女自身でさえそれを知らない。それを知りたいといつも思ってる。: Even she herself doesn't know. And she always wants to find out.
天使や精霊、それこそ神さまとしか呼びようのない“何か”であろうと俺は感じてしまう: Because I can't help feeling that she's an angel, a spirit, or "something" that can only be called a god--without trying to be clever about it, I also call her "God."
『気づいたらここにいた』: "'Before I knew it, I was here.'"
――出会ったばかりのナナちゃんは俺にそう言ったのだった。: --That was what Nana-chan told me when we had just met.
『……気づいたら私は、この列車と一緒にここにいて』: "'...Before I knew it, I was here together with this train.'"
『ここから、この、列車の中から一歩も外へ出られない、そんな私は……“夜”の世界を: "'Unable to take even a single step outside of this place, outside of this train... I have lived on by wandering from heart to heart of all the people living in the world of the "Night."'"
ずっと昔、俺たちはこの蒸気機関車に乗ってたくさん、たくさんの“夜”の世界を越えて: A long time ago, we rode this steam locomotive across many, many worlds of the "Night" and arrived at this town of cherry blossoms.
だから俺は、この“夜”の世界で、彼女がどんな“役割”を担っているのかを知っている: That's why I know what kind of "role" she plays in this world of the "Night."
だからこそ俺は、この“ぬいぐるみ”を。: That is precisely why I brought this "stuffed animal."
……“悪夢”と化した誰かの“心”を。: Someone's "heart" that had turned into a "nightmare."
……この子はとても、やさしい子: "...This child is a very kind child."
俺が手渡した“ぬいぐるみ”を、そっとナナちゃんは抱き寄せた。: Nana-chan gently hugged the "stuffed animal" I handed to her.
だけど少しばかりやさしすぎたのだ、と。: But she was just a little too kind, she says.
抱きしめた“誰か”の心にあった想いを、言葉に変えて――語り始める。: Turning the feelings inside the heart of the "someone" she was holding into words--she begins to tell the story.
誰もが彼女に甘えた。学校の先生も。近所の人も。……両親さえも: "Everyone took advantage of her kindness. Her teachers at school. The neighbors. ...Even her parents."
だけど何があってもこの子は、[・|女][・|の][・|子]は、笑ってた。: But no matter what happened, this child, this *girl*, kept smiling.
だから、“この子には何をしても許される”……。言葉はなくとも、どうしてだろう、自: "So, 'No matter what you do to this child, she'll forgive you'... Even without words, I wonder why, she naturally ended up in that kind of role."
何をしても、何をしなくても、笑顔で許してくれる彼女に、いつしか誰も“ごめんなさい: No matter what anyone did, or didn't do, she would forgive them with a smile, so before long, nobody said "I'm sorry" or "Thank you" to her anymore. Nor did they even feel that way.
……だから女の子は、お父さんに、お母さんに……大切だった、ふたりに。何の説明もな: "...So even when the girl was abandoned without any explanation by her father, and her mother... by the two people so precious to her, she kept smiling."
まずお父さんが家に帰ってこなくなった。: First, her father stopped coming home.
“お父さんには私たち以外に別の家族があって、そちらのほうが大切になってしまったの: "'Your father has another family besides us, and they've become more important to him'--"
あの子のお母さんはそう言って泣いていた。: That child's mother cried as she said that.
……女の子も。まるで自分のことのように涙を流して悲しんだ: "...The girl, too, shed tears and grieved as if it were happening to her own self."
これからはふたり一緒に力を合わせて生きていこう……。: From now on, the two of them would work together and live on...
そう、思っていたのに……。: Even though that was what she had thought...
お母さんも別の家族を見つけて、女の子の待つ家に帰ってこなくなってしまった: "Her mother also found another family, and stopped coming back to the home where the girl was waiting."
真冬のことだ。: It was in the dead of winter.
電気も水も停められて……。: The electricity and water were shut off...
女の子は肌を突き刺す空気の寒さと、心を突き刺すさみしさと、どうしようもない空腹で: "With the freezing air piercing her skin, the loneliness piercing her heart, and a helpless hunger, the girl feels as though she might fade away at any moment."
だけど女の子は決して、両親を責めるようなことはしなかった。むしろ自分が悪いのだと: Yet the girl never once blamed her parents. Instead, she thought it was her own fault.
……お父さん。お母さん。ふたりが帰ってきてくれないのは、私が、誕生日に買ってもら: "...Dad. Mom. The reason the two of you won't come home is because I'm a bad girl who lost the teddy bear you bought me for my birthday."
そんなふうに、思ってしまっていた。: That was what she had ended up believing.
……それは両親の教育の結果なのかもしれない: "...Perhaps that was the result of how her parents raised her."
“人の痛みを自分の痛みのように思いなさい”――: "Think of others' pain as your own"--
あなたがつらいとき、周りの人はもっともっと、あなたよりももっと、つらいのだから…: "When you are hurting, the people around you are hurting much, much more than you are..."
だからいつでも笑顔でいなさい。: So always keep a smile on your face.
どんなことをされたとしても、相手を笑顔で、許してあげなさい: "No matter what is done to you, forgive the other person with a smile."
決して相手を恨んだり、責めるようなことをしてはだめ。: You must never resent or blame the other person.
……たとえば、あなたを殴りつけた誰かは、もっともっと、心も身体も、あなたよりもず: "...For instance, someone who hits you is feeling much, much more pain in their heart and body than you ever are--"
それが両親からうけた教育だった。: That was the upbringing she received from her parents.
――“相手の痛みのわかる大人になりなさい。そうでなければ、みんなあなたを愛せない: "--'Grow up to be an adult who understands the pain of others. Otherwise, nobody will be able to love you.'"
どうして“バカみたい”と言えるのか――それを論じることさえもバカみたい。: Even arguing about why it can be called "ridiculous" is ridiculous in itself.
女の子の心を都合よく操るための暴論でしかない――きっとそれを唱えた本人等もそのこ: It's nothing more than an absurd argument meant to conveniently manipulate the girl's heart--so absurd that the very people who preached it probably didn't even realize it themselves.
……女の子は、お母さんが新しい家族と暮らしている家を一度だけ見に行った: "...Just once, the girl went to see the house where her mother was living with her new family."
たくさんの笑顔が似合うクリスマス……。: Christmas, a time meant for so many smiles...
暖かそうな明かりの洩れている窓を覗いた。: She peeked through the window where a warm-looking light was spilling out.
お母さんは知らない女の子にやさしく微笑みかけていた。: Her mother was smiling gently at an unfamiliar girl.
女の子の大好きだったその手で、知らない女の子の頭を撫でていた: "With that hand the girl had loved so much, she was stroking the unfamiliar girl's head."
“よかったねお母さん。本当に”: "'I'm so glad for you, Mom. Really.'"
このごろずっと、お母さん、つらそうだったから……。: Because lately, Mom had looked like she was in so much pain...
笑えているのなら、よかった。: If she's able to smile, then I'm glad.
“……でも、どうしてかな、お母さん。心が痛いよ。とても、とても……”: "'...But I wonder why, Mom. My heart hurts. So, so much...'"
でも、ずっと、ずっと、その場を離れられず、立ち尽くしていた。: But for a long, long time, she couldn't leave that spot, standing there frozen.
……お母さん。だめだよ。そんな顔、見たくない: "...Mom. Don't. I don't want to see you make a face like that."
お母さんの隣には、“この子、だあれ？”と首を傾げる女の子。その手には、ぬいぐるみ: "Next to her mother was the girl tilting her head and asking, 'Who's this?' And in her hand was a stuffed animal..."
なくしてしまったと思っていた、お誕生日のプレゼント。: The birthday present she thought she had lost.
“相手の痛みのわかる大人になりなさい。そうでなければ、みんなあなたを愛せない”―: "Grow up to be an adult who understands the pain of others. Otherwise, nobody will be able to love you"--she heard that voice coming from somewhere.
だから女の子は大丈夫だよと笑って見せた。: So the girl smiled and told her that she was okay.
私も、お母さん、私も……新しい家族を見つけたの: "Me too, Mom, I... I found a new family, too."
だからお母さん、大丈夫だから、私、平気だから……: "So Mom, it's okay, I'm completely fine..."
だからお母さん、そんな、悲しそうな顔、しないで――: So Mom, please don't make such a sad face--
でも、誰も、追いかけてきてはくれなかった。: But nobody came chasing after her.
本当に“大丈夫”だと思われた。本当に“平気”だと、安心された。……“私には何をし: "She really believed I was 'okay.' She was relieved, thinking I was truly 'fine.' ...'Anything done to me will be forgiven.' Strangely enough, everyone ends up thinking that way. For some reason, that's the role I'm always stuck playing."
そんなことないのに。: Even though that wasn't true at all.
大丈夫なはず、ないのに。: Even though there was no way she could be okay.
お母さん。お父さん。ふたりの幸せには私は邪魔だと女の子は気づいた。: Mom. Dad. The girl realized that she was in the way of their happiness.

足りていないからこそ俺は未だに“夜の国”の中で“魔法”を十全と扱うことができない: It is precisely because they are missing that I still cannot fully wield "magic" within the "Land of Night."
なぜなら俺たちが使える“魔法”は“想像力”であるからだ――“想像力”とは心の力だ: Because the "magic" we can use is "imagination"--and "imagination" is the power of the heart. The color of the heart. The pattern of the heart.
それらが欠落してしまっている歴然とした証拠が、自身の未熟さとしていつも、いつでも: The undeniable proof that those things are missing stands before my eyes always, at every moment, in the form of my own inadequacy.
本当は、クロ。俺はさ……海底のポストから“[手紙|願い]”を回収したときも: "The truth is, Kuro... even when we collected the 'wishes' from the mailbox at the bottom of the sea..."
その手紙からふわりとこぼれた“誰か”の願いに、心で触れた、あのときも: "Even when my heart touched 'someone's' wish that softly spilled out from those letters..."
……みんなが、“[あの子|ぬいぐるみ]”を見送ったそのときも: "...And even when everyone saw 'that stuffed animal' off..."
悲しんだり神妙なそぶりをして見せてはいたけれど……その実。: I put on an act of being sad and solemn... but in reality...
俺は、泣けなかったどころじゃない。たぶんほんの少しも、[・|し][・|ん][・|: "Not only could I not cry, I probably couldn't even feel the slightest bit solemn."
そんなヘドロのような心の持ち主で、あるからこそ。: It's precisely because I possess a heart like sludge.
[・|こ][・|ん][・|な][・|自][・|分]がつくづく嫌いだと感じてしまう: I feel so thoroughly disgusted with this side of myself. Because I hate it. Because I despise it. That's why I want to run away from a guy like myself, and yet... Of course, something like that is impossible.
ならばもう、この命を自ら手放すくらいしか、問題解決の方法はどこにもないのではない: In that case, isn't letting go of this life with my own hands the only way left anywhere to solve the problem...?
これ以上は何も言えない。: I couldn't say anything more than this.
今は、言えない。: Right now, I couldn't say it.
少しの沈黙。ちくたく、ちくたく、時計の音ばかりが耳に痛い。普段はまったく気になら: A brief silence. Tick-tock, tick-tock--only the sound of the clock grated painfully on my ears. Even though it was a faint sound I normally wouldn't notice at all.
……でも、大雅。知らない子のことを心から心配できないと、きみは、言うけど: "...But, Taiga. You say you can't truly worry about a girl you don't know..."
自分のことばかりを心配している自分のことが、きみは嫌いだと、そう言うけれど: "And you say you hate yourself for only ever worrying about yourself..."
きみはハルのことを、本気で気にかけていたように……わたしには思えたよ: "To me... it seemed like you genuinely cared about Haru."
“刻の終着駅”からの帰り道。: On the way back from the "Terminal of Time."
ハルとふたりで夜空を見つめながら心について少しだけ、言葉を交換し合った。: While gazing up at the night sky together, Haru and I had exchanged just a few words about the heart.
そのときのことを実際に見ていられたわたしじゃ、ないけれど……でも: "It's not as though I was actually there to see it happen... but still."
明日を怖がるハルに大丈夫だよって、大雅はそう言ったんだよね？ 明日のハルが笑顔で: "When Haru was afraid of tomorrow, you told her it would be okay, didn't you, Taiga? You wished that Haru would be able to smile tomorrow, didn't you...?"
知らない誰かのために本気で悩めなくても。大切な……大切だと思いたい友だちのためな: "Even if you can't genuinely agonize over someone you don't know... for the sake of a precious friend--a friend you want to hold dear--you can agonize right alongside them with everything you have."
今はそれで、充分。むしろ上出来だってわたしは大雅にそう言いたい: "It's plenty for now. In fact, I want to tell you that you did more than well enough, Taiga."
驚いているのだ。とても、とても。: I was surprised. Truly, deeply surprised.
いつもこうして電話で話すときは、少しだけ素直になってくれるクロだけれど……。: Whenever we talk on the phone like this, Kuro always becomes just a little bit more honest with me, and yet...
それにしても今夜の君は饒舌だと感じてしまう。: Even so, I couldn't help feeling that you were unusually talkative tonight.
クロとこうして話せるのは素直にうれしい。言いようのない安心感がある。: Being able to talk with Kuro like this made me genuinely happy. It gave me an indescribable sense of relief.
それは、幼い頃のことを、小さな君よりももっとずっと小さかった頃のことを……。: Because it made me remember when we were little--when I was much, much smaller even than the tiny you are now...
列車にガタンゴトンと揺られながら、君に膝枕をしてもらい……心地よくうたた寝をして: Resting my head in your lap as the train clattered and swayed along... comfortably dozing off.
ふと、君の言葉が途切れていたことに、気付く。: Suddenly, I realized your words had cut off.
名前を呼ぶと、『ううう』、と小さな唸り声。: When I called her name, I heard a tiny groan: "Uuu..."
何か、あったの……と、俺は焦りを覚える。: Did something happen...? A sense of panic washed over me.
しかしクロは呼びかけに答えない――うううという唸り声。: However, Kuro didn't answer my call--only letting out another "Uuu..." groan.
そして耳を澄ませば聞こえてくるのは、: And when I strained my ears, what I heard was...
という、小さな、とても小さく微かな、クロのつぶやきだった。: It was a small, a very small and faint mutter from Kuro.
――ぽつりと一言、クロの声。: --A single murmured word in Kuro's voice.
なぜだかどきりと、俺の心は小さく爆ぜる。: For some reason, my heart gave a sudden, tiny jolt.
思いもよらずおどおどとした声が返ってくる。: Unexpectedly, a timid, flustered voice came back.
ちょっと……その、……ううっ……色々: "Just... um... uuu... a lot of things."
色々、と……調子に乗って……話しすぎてしまった……かも: "A lot of things, like... getting carried away... and maybe talking a little too much..."
もにょもにょと萎んでいく声だった。: Her voice trailed off into an embarrassed mumble, shrinking away.
息をのむ気配が伝わってきた。: I could hear her catch her breath.
うー、とか。あ、ああ……とか。うっ、あっ、ああああ……っ、だとか。: Sounds like "Uuu..." and "A-Aaah..." and "Ugh, ah, aaaah..."
電話越しに聞こえてくるその声には。: Hearing her voice over the phone like that...
――ごろごろごろごろ、転げまわっている……。: --And rolling around and around on the floor...
そんなクロの姿を思い浮かべ、俺は……、: Picturing Kuro acting like that, I...
[まぶた|瞼]の裏に思い浮かべたクロの姿は、その様子は、本当の君とどれほど被って: I didn't know how closely the image of Kuro behind my eyelids matched the real you, though.
まるで的外れな妄想を、俺が勝手に思い浮かべてはニマニマしているだかだろうけれど…: For all I knew, I was just grinning to myself over some completely off-the-mark delusion I'd conjured up...
それでも俺は、頬がどうしようもなく緩むのを止められなかった。: Even so, I couldn't stop my cheeks from breaking into a helpless smile.
目を細めたかのようなクロの声だ。: Kuro's voice sounded like she was narrowing her eyes at me.
かわいい唸り声もぴたりと止まる。: Her cute little groans stopped dead in their tracks, too.
何かを察したようにクロが言ったのだ。: Kuro asked, as if she had sensed something.
大雅。今、わたしのこと……笑った？: "Taiga. Did you just... laugh at me?"
意地悪な大雅は、嫌いだな。眠れず弱気になってる大雅のほうが……少しだけ、かわいい: "I don't like it when you're being mean, Taiga. You're... a little bit cuter when you can't sleep and get all timid."
ごめん。ごめんね。もう笑わないよ: "Sorry. I'm sorry. I won't laugh anymore."
笑いをぐっと堪えてそう言うと――クロはもう一度、ため息。: When I stifled my laughter and said that--Kuro let out another sigh.
これじゃあ、今夜……わたしのほうが眠れなくなってしまいそう。……てれてれしちゃっ: "At this rate... I feel like I'm the one who won't be able to sleep tonight. ...Because I'm all bashful-washful now."
まるで近くで見ているみたいだと冗談めかして言ってみる。: I said it jokingly, as if she were watching me from somewhere nearby.
しどろもどろだった。少しだけ。: She stumbled over her words. Just a little.
案外本当に近くにいてくれるのかも。そんなことを思う。: Maybe she really was somewhere close by after all. The thought crossed my mind.
すると……不思議だ。: And when it did... it was strange.
今夜、俺はひとりじゃないかも。そう錯覚できた。: It gave me the illusion that maybe I wasn't alone tonight.
ふわりと心が[・|ぼ][・|や][・|け][・|た]気がした。: I felt my mind gently blur and soften.
……粘つく“夜”色が解けた、気がした。: I felt as though the sticky color of the "night" had melted away.
それは睡魔の足音だ。: Those were the approaching footsteps of sleep.
胸に、心に、頭の中に、今もこびり付いてる[・|問][・|題]は、解決できていない: Even though the problem still clinging to my chest, my heart, and my head wasn't anywhere near solved--in fact, I hadn't even managed to squeeze out anything resembling an answer.
だからこそ今夜の俺は、さっきまでの、この俺は、眠れずうんうん唸ってばかりいたはず: And even though that was the exact reason I couldn't sleep tonight, groaning and agonizing over it until just a moment ago.
それなのにクロと少し笑いあえた、それだけで……、: Despite all that, just sharing a little laugh with Kuro was enough to...
……そんな俺を、やっぱり近くで見ていてくれてるのだろうか。: Was she really watching over me from somewhere close by right now?
ふっと微笑むかのような、声で、: In a voice that sounded like she was smiling softly,
……さみしいことがいっぱいの夜は、楽しいことだけいっぱい、たくさん、考えていれば: "...On nights filled with lonely things, all you have to do is think about lots and lots of fun things instead."
悲しいことは知らないふりをするみたいにね。: Just like pretending not to know about the sad things.
見上げた夜空のきらきら星を、ふたりで一緒に、数えるみたいにね。: Just like the two of us counting the twinkling stars in the night sky together.
……大雅の夢は、大雅の未来は……いっぱいのきらきらで、色づくよ: "...Your dreams, Taiga, and your future... will be colored with lots and lots of sparkles."
……そして俺は、つくづく、君とこうして話すのが好きなんだなあと、思うから――: And because I realized all over again just how much I loved talking with you like this--
君と一緒に、すばらしい明日という時間について“想像”してみようと……心でそっと、: I decided to try "imagining" that wonderful time called tomorrow together with you... and quietly took a deep breath in my heart.
きっと、君がどこかで見守っていてくれる、俺の、明日という時間は。: That time called tomorrow, which you would surely be watching over from somewhere.
……こんな感じになるだろうと、思うのだ。: I thought to myself that it would probably go something like this.
真っ暗闇の中に、ひとひら。: A single petal in the pitch-black darkness.
薄桃色の花びらが、ふわふわ、はらりと舞ったのだ。: A pale pink petal danced and drifted gently down.
その、たったひとつの春色が。: And when that single touch of spring color...
暗闇のスクリーンに波紋を落とすように、弾けて、消えると――: Burst and vanished, casting ripples across the dark screen--
『……大雅くん。私、やっぱり怖い。かも』: "'...Taiga-kun. I think I'm scared after all. Maybe.'"
『私。胸がどきどき、どきどき、大変だよ……』: "'My heart is pounding and pounding so hard, it's awful...'"
ぽつり、ぽつりと落とされたその声で。: With those words, dropped one by one...
真っ暗闇でしかなかったはずの背景が……光景が、ほんの些細な“魔法”で、色づいてい: The background, the scenery that had been nothing but pitch-black darkness... began to take on color through a tiny little bit of "magic"--
満開のさくらと、吹雪く花びらに包まれて……。: Enveloped by cherry blossoms in full bloom, and a swirling blizzard of petals...
さくらの森へと続く長い、長い、階段をふたりでのぼるその途中。: Halfway up the long, long staircase leading to the cherry blossom forest, as the two of us climbed together.
うつむいた彼女は、ぎゅっと[まぶた|瞼]を閉じていた。: Looking down, she squeezed her eyelids shut.
何が怖いのかと問いかけてみる。: I asked her what she was afraid of.
すると立ち止まってしまっていた彼女は、ふるふると首を振り、: Having stopped in her tracks, she gave a trembling shake of her head,
『みんなに忘れられてたらどうしよう』: "'What if everyone has forgotten about me?'"
『ちゃんとお話しできなかったら、どうしよう』: "'What if I can't talk to them properly?'"
『そう、思うと……やっぱりすごく、とても、とても……怖いんだよ』: "'When I think about that... it really is super, very, very... scary.'"
明日の俺は、きっとあの子の手を引き、この階段をのぼるだろう。: Tomorrow, I would surely take her hand and climb these stairs.
積み重なる一段、一段が続いていくその先を、俺は、あの子と一緒に――少し怖がりな女: Together with her--together with that slightly timid girl, Hiiragi Haru--I would look up at what lay beyond the steps piling up one after another.
俺はハルを振り向いて――笑いかけてみる。: I turned back toward Haru--and offered her a smile.
そう言う俺に、ハルは不器用に笑うのだ。: At my words, Haru gave an awkward smile.
不安そうに。心配そうに。口元だけで、微笑む。: Anxiously. Worriedly. Smiling only with the corners of her mouth.
……その笑顔を[・|本][・|当]にするにはどうしたらいいだろう。: What could I do to make that smile real?
柊ハル。彼女は引っ込み思案な女の子。: Hiiragi Haru. She was a shy, reserved girl.
いつも笑顔であろうとがんばってはいるけれど……その実。: She always tried her hardest to keep a smile on her face... but in truth...
その胸の中はどきどき、どきどき、痛いくらいに高鳴っていて……。: The heart inside her chest was pounding, pounding so hard it almost hurt...
だけど彼女はちょっとかわいい意地っ張り。: Even so, she had a cute, stubborn streak.
自分の不安やどきどきを、絶対ぜったい悟られまいと、悟られては格好悪いと……恥ずか: Determined never, ever to let anyone notice her anxiety or her racing heart--thinking it would be uncool and embarrassing if they did--she put on a smile once again.
その明るさの下にあるもうひとつの柊ハルを、その心を、彼女はなぜだか俺にだけ、垣間: For some reason, I was the only one she allowed to catch a glimpse of that other Hiiragi Haru, the heart hidden beneath her cheerful exterior.
『大丈夫。平気だ。心配しなくていい。……そばに、いるから』: "'It's okay. You'll be fine. You don't have to worry. ...Because I'm right here with you.'"
俺はそんな言葉で勇気づけたいと、願うのだ。: And so, I wished to encourage her with those words.
『いつの間にか特別なんかじゃ、なくなってしまったとしても』: "'Even if, before we know it, we stop being special at all.'"
『少女時代が終わり、特別な日々の記憶も少しずつ薄くなっていき……』: "'Even if girlhood comes to an end, and the memories of our special days fade away little by little...'"
『代わりに、不安や心配やさみしさばかりが横たわる――そんな大人の世界に、手招きさ: "'And in their place, an adult world filled with nothing but anxiety, worry, and loneliness beckons to us.'"
『……世界中の誰もがみんな、君たちのことを、君たちの“魔法”のことを忘れてしまっ: "'...Even if everyone in the whole world forgets about all of you, and about your "magic."'"
『かつて君たちが誰より、何より、勇気のある女の子たちだったんだって』: "'That once upon a time, you were all girls with more courage than anyone or anything else.'"
だから、できる。: That's why you can do it.
君にならできる。君たちになら、何でもできる。: You can do it. All of you can do anything.
つらくて大変な日々を乗り越えて、今日まで生きてきたんじゃないか。: After all, haven't you overcome such painful, difficult days to live up until today?
そういうふうに俺は、彼女を……彼女たちを、応援し続けていたいから……。: Because in that way, I want to keep cheering her--cheering all of them--on...
『さあ、行こうか。みんなハルを、待ってるよ』: "'Come on, let's go. Everyone is waiting for you, Haru.'"
そうして俺は彼女の手を引き。: With that, I took her hand.
ひとつ、ふたつ、しっかりと石の階段をのぼり。: One step, two steps, we climbed firmly up the stone stairs.
そんなみんなの声を、期待しながら。: Hoping to hear everyone's voices saying just that.
まずそう言ったのは姫織だった。: The first to say so was Himeori.
それが合図だったみたいにたくさん、たくさんの花びらが、吹き抜けた風に乗り舞いあが: As if that were the signal, countless, countless petals rode the blowing wind and danced up into the air.
一瞬だけ目を閉じて、恐る恐る、開く。: Closing my eyes for just an instant, I timidly opened them again.
『わわわ……っ、お弁当に埃が入っちゃいますっ』: "'Wawawa...! Dust is gonna get in the bento!'"
『うおおっ、大変だっ、あさひさんが作ってくれたおむすびに花びらがっ』: "'Whoa, this is bad! Petals are getting on the rice balls Asahi-san made for us!'"
『ふわぁ……すごい。ひらひらで、ぽかぽかで、ふわふわだよ、お姉ちゃん』: "'Fwaah... amazing. It's all fluttery, warm, and fluffy, Onee-chan.'"
『そうだなあ。うん。お昼寝がまんして来てよかったなあ』: "'It sure is. Yeah. I'm glad I held off on my afternoon nap to come here.'"
珍しく十夜やあさひさんまで。: Unusually enough, even Toya and Asahi-san were present.
たどり着いたのは姫織の神社だ。: The place we had arrived at was Himeori's shrine.
明日の放課後。あるいは学校を抜け出して集まったお昼の時間。: Tomorrow after school. Or perhaps during lunch break, having snuck out of school to gather together.
さくらの木々に包まれた石畳の境内は、春が満開に咲き乱れ……。: The stone-paved shrine grounds, surrounded by cherry trees, were bursting in full spring bloom...
みんなが持ち寄ったお弁当や、色とりどりの駄菓子が溢れ。: Overflowing with the boxed lunches everyone had brought and colorful, cheap sweets.
約束通りのお花見会が催されているその場所に、: In that place where the promised flower-viewing party was being held,
ハルの緊張しっぱなしの声が、響いた。: Haru's thoroughly nervous voice rang out.
『今日から、ど、どうか……また……っ、よろしくお願い、します……っ』: "'Starting today, p-please... once again... take good care of me...!'"
噛みながらも小さく叫ぶようにして言い、ハルは勢いよく頭を下げた。: Stumbling over her words as she practically shouted in a small voice, Haru bowed her head vigorously.
……そんなハルにみんなは顔を見合わせ、そして、微笑む。: Seeing Haru like that, everyone exchanged glances and smiled.
誰かが“おかえりなさい”と、そっとやさしい言葉をくれた。: Someone gently offered the kind words, "Welcome back."
だから俺も。……柊ハル。彼女のことを振り返り、: So I did, too. ...Looking back at her, at Hiiragi Haru,
『恥ずかしいことを言うようだけど……今日だけは特別だ。ハル。こんな日が来るのをず: "'This might sound embarrassing to say, but... today is special. Haru. I've been waiting and waiting for a day like this to come.'"
思えば今日まで言いそびれていた“おかえり”の言葉を、俺もなんとかここで手渡せた。: Come to think of it, I managed to finally hand over the "welcome back" I had missed the chance to say until today, right here. Along with the same smile as everyone else.
そんな俺にちょっと驚いたような顔をしたけれど、: She looked a little surprised at me for a moment,
穏やかさを取り戻し、ふと――桜色のその頬を緩める。: Regaining her composure, her cherry-blossom-pink cheeks suddenly relaxed into a smile.
暖かな季節が寝転ぶこの町に、またひとつ、新しい春がやって来て……。: To this town where the warm season lay sprawled out, another new spring had arrived...
クロもさくらの木からちらちらと顔を出している。: Kuro was also peeking her face out from behind a cherry tree.
そんな様子に思わず吹き出す。: Seeing her like that, I couldn't help but burst into laughter.
クロは俺の背中に隠れるみたいにして、小さな身体を寄せたのだ。: Kuro pressed her small body close, as if hiding behind my back.
柊ハルよりも重度の人見知りが、ぼそぼそと、言った。俺にしか聞こえないように。: Someone with an even more severe case of shyness than Hiiragi Haru murmured softly, so that only I could hear.
『……今日はね、いつもより、とびきり甘い……チョコがいい』: "'...Today, you know, I want chocolate... that's much, much sweeter than usual.'"
あ～ん、と開けられた小さな口に、ひとかけら。: Into the small mouth opened wide with an "aah," I popped a single piece.
俺も笑って、クロを見つめる――ニヤニヤと纏わりつくたくさんの視線には、気付かない: I smiled too and gazed at Kuro--pretending not to notice the many grinning stares clinging to us.
こんな時間も悪くはないはず。: A time like this wouldn't be bad at all.
望む未来を闇色の心のスクリーンに映し出すこと。: To project the future I wished for onto the dark-colored screen of my heart.
そうすれば世界はきっと変わっていくはずだった。: If I did that, the world would surely change.
誰もが使える“夜”の魔法。: The magic of the "Night" that anyone could use.
明日の光景を盗み見たかのように、今夜俺が思い描いこの光景は。: This scene I envisioned tonight, as if stealing a glimpse of tomorrow's scenery.
まあ、たぶん、半分くらいは本当に叶ってくれるのでは、ないだろうか――: Well, maybe about half of it would actually come true, wouldn't it--?
きみの未来にたくさん、たくさん、きらきらの星が降ることを……わたしはそれだけを、: That lots and lots of sparkling stars will fall upon your future... that's the only thing I'm always picturing in my mind, after all.
俺の“夜の魔法”はいつか、君の口癖みたいな“さよなら”までをも、叶えてしまうので: Wouldn't my "magic of the Night" someday grant even that "goodbye" of yours, which you say like a habit?

昔は昔だけど。今は今、だけれど……。あんなにもずるっこなことが堂々と許されちゃっ: "The past is the past, and the present is the present, though... Is it really okay to let something so unfair slide right out in the open? No, that's no good. This is a problem."
ええ、そうです。問題です。大問題です。だからこちらも何か作戦を考えておかなきゃい: "Yes, that's right. It's a problem. A huge problem. Which means we need to come up with a strategy of our own."
君たちは何をひそひそ話しているんだい……聞こえちゃってるけどさ: "What are you two whispering about over there...? I can hear you, you know."
――あ、今ので何か、思い出したかもしれない: "--Ah, hearing that just now might've reminded me of something."
ふと、突然に智仁が声を上げた。: Out of nowhere, Tomohito suddenly spoke up.
昔々の私たちがここで探していた……？: "The one we were looking for here a long, long time ago...?"
俺たちさ、昔もここで、今と同じような会話をしたような気がするんだよ――……: "I feel like we had this exact same conversation right here a long time ago, too--..."
『ねえねえ、ひよちゃん。この神社でおみくじ買うと、神さまにお願い聞いてもらえるっ: "Hey, hey, Hiyo-chan. Is it true that if you buy a fortune slip at this shrine, God will grant your wish?"
『そう言われていますね。子どもの間でも。大人の間でも』: "So they say. Both among children and among adults."
『あ、それって……あれだよね。参禅町の七不思議のひとつだ』: "Ah, that's... that thing, right? One of the Seven Mysteries of Sanzen Town."
『そうそう。確か……ええっと。この神社で売られてる特別なおみくじを買うと、夢の中: "Right, right. If I remember correctly... um. If you buy a special fortune slip sold at this shrine, you can meet the guardian deity of this town in your dreams..."
『その神さまと夢の中で仲良くなれたら、お願いごとを叶えてもらえる。そんな噂でした: "And if you make friends with that deity in your dream, they'll grant your wish. Wasn't that the rumor...?"
『うん、そうだよ。そんな噂で、そんな“七不思議”のひとつ、だったんだよ』: "Mhm, that's right. That was the rumor, and it was one of the 'Seven Mysteries.'"
『むむむ。その噂は[・|私][・|た][・|ち][・|が][・|検][・|証]し: "Hmm. *We might need to investigate* that rumor ourselves."
『……ううん、ハルちゃん。たぶんね。その神さまのこと、私たちたぶん知ってるよね』: "...No, Haru-chan. Probably... we probably already know that deity, don't we?"
『え？ ……あっ、そうか。うん、そうだよね。だってその神さまって、きっと――』: "Huh? ...Ah, right. Yeah, you're right. Because that deity is definitely--"
くすくすと声を殺して笑いあうかつての俺たち――……: Our past selves stifled our giggles as we laughed together--...
『じゃ、買っちゃおう。おみくじ買って、今夜も神さまとお話ししよう。この町の神さま: "Then let's buy some! Let's buy fortune slips and talk to God tonight, too. The deity of this town is always all alone, so I'm sure they'll be happy if we go visit."
『うーん。どうかなあ。あの神さまは人見知りだから……』: "Hmm. I wonder. That deity is pretty shy around strangers, so..."
『おみくじ買うより、カップ麺いっぱい持って行ったほうが、あの神さまは喜びそうです: "Rather than buying fortune slips, I feel like that deity would be happier if we brought a bunch of cup noodles."
『んー。おみくじ、お姉ちゃん買おうかなあ。おこずかい今月きびしいけど』: "Hmm. Maybe Big Sis will buy a fortune slip, too. Even though my allowance is tight this month."
『神社もお寺も、神さまだって。“ぼらんちぃあ”でご利益ばら撒いてるわけじゃあねぇ: "Shrines, temples, and even the gods themselves aren't handing out blessings as 'vuh-lun-teers,' you know."
『おおー、ひよちゃんが突然難しい言葉を』: "Whoa, Hiyo-chan suddenly busted out a big word."
『もしも“噂”通り、おみくじ買って、小さな神さまがお願いを聞いてくれるとしたら…: "If the 'rumor' is true, and buying a fortune slip means the little god will grant your wish... what would everyone wish for?"
あくまで百円程度で叶えられる“お願い”であって……、: Still, it would only be a "wish" that could be granted for about a hundred yen...
それは、“魔法”を必要とする“夢”の話では、もちろんないけど……、: And of course, we weren't talking about the kind of "dream" that required "magic," either...
『えー……、お願いは人に教えちゃだめって気がしますけど』: "Ehh... I feel like you're not supposed to tell other people your wish, though."
『“大雅くんがくーちゃんばっかり贔屓しなくなりますように”』: "'I wish Taiga-kun would stop playing favorites with Kuu-chan all the time.'"
『えへへ。あだ名っていいよね。なんだか仲良しだよーって感じがね、すっごく伝わって: "Ehehe. Nicknames are nice, aren't they? They really get across the feeling that you're super close friends... Wait, huh?"
『お顔が真っ青。大変』: "Your face is completely pale. Oh dear."
『えっと……クロちゃんは、くーちゃん。今決めました。そして姫織ちゃんはひよちゃん: "Um... Kuro-chan is Kuu-chan. I just decided that now. And Himeori-chan is Hiyo-chan. Chiwa-chan is small and cute, so she's Chiwakkoi--"
『……それ、やめてほしいっていつも言ってるのに』: "...I always tell you to stop calling me that, though."
『――あれ？ あれれ？ おかしいよ？ 私だけ……女の子の中で、私だけ、あだ名がな: "--Huh? Wait a second? That's weird! Only me... Out of all the girls, I'm the only one without a nickname!"
『い、いやいや。それはなんだかさすがに変じゃないかなあ』: "N-No, wait. Isn't that jumping to conclusions a bit?"
『百円！ おみくじ買って、小さなちいさな神さまに、悪い子な大雅を叱ってもらわなき: "One hundred yen! I have to buy a fortune slip and get the tiny, tiny god to scold bad-boy Taiga...!"
なんだ。思い出したって……殆ど“噂話”と関係ないじゃないか。ただの思い出話だ: "What the heck? You said you remembered something, but... that had almost nothing to do with the 'rumor.' That was just a random memory."
何を言うんだ親友。思い出は、宝物だろ？ 思い出してみろよ。今の俺たちがしているこ: "What are you talking about, my best friend? Memories are treasures, right? Think about it. What is it that we're doing right now? A treasure hunt, isn't it?"
得意そうにそんなことを言うのだ――少しイラッとした。: He said it so smugly--it ticked me off a little.
俺たちは姫織の巫女服姿を写真に撮ってみたり、お茶を美味しくいただいてみたりして…: We took some photos of Himeori in her shrine maiden outfit, enjoyed some delicious tea, and then...
次の場所へ移動する。: We moved on to the next place.
おみくじは今日のところは引かずにおいた。: We decided not to draw any fortune slips for today.
俺たちの町、参禅町の中心には河が流れている。: A river runs through the center of our town, Sanzen Town.
河川と呼ぶにはこじんまりとしていて、小川と呼ぶには大層な設備で環境を整備されてい: It was a bit too cozy to be called a proper river, yet its banks were too heavily developed and maintained to be called a mere stream.
さくら並木に囲まれたその河に、町は大きくふたつに分断されているけれど……。: Lined with rows of cherry trees, the river roughly divides the town in two, but...
いくつかの小さな石造りの橋が、あちら側とこちら側を繋いでいた。: Several small stone bridges connected this side to the other.
その内のひとつに俺たちは立っている。: We were standing on one of them.
この橋は通学路として今も昔もよく利用していたるだが……。: We'd used this bridge a lot as a route to school both now and in the past, though...
ここにはどんな“不思議”があったかなあ。俺たち。この橋をよく行ったり来たりしてい: "I wonder what kind of 'mystery' was here. I feel like we used to walk back and forth across this bridge a lot."
みんなと違って俺は昔のことをそれなりに覚えてはいる。: Unlike everyone else, I remembered the past reasonably well.
俺たちの“昔”には、大人の時間に持ち込めない多くの記憶で溢れてる――故に。: Our "past" is overflowing with many memories that can't be brought into adulthood--and therefore,
大人になり始めているみんなには、当時の思い出が薄いのは無理からぬこと。: It was only natural that everyone else, who were starting to become adults, had only faint memories of that time.
まだまだ心も身体も大人になれないこの俺が、みんなよりその記憶を色濃く持つのもまた: And it was equally natural that I, who still couldn't become an adult in mind or body, held onto those memories more vividly than the others.
だが、それはあくまでも[・|そ][・|れ][・|な][・|り]でしかない。: However, I only remembered them *reasonably* well.
何をしようとしていたのかは思い出せても、実際に何をしていたのか……その細部はみん: Even if I could remember what we were trying to do, what we actually did... those details were just as hazy for me as they were for everyone else.
だからこの場所に立ち、でこぼことした記憶の溝を洗い出そうと懸命になる。: That's why I stood in this place, trying desperately to uncover the bumpy grooves of my memory.
手すりにもたれかかり、足元を流れる河の水面を見下ろした。: I leaned against the railing and looked down at the surface of the river flowing beneath my feet.
はらはらと降り注ぐさくらの花びらが、水面に微かな波紋を広げ……ゆっくりと流れ去っ: Gently falling cherry blossom petals spread faint ripples across the water's surface... and slowly drifted away.
人通りもそれなりに多いから、小さな子がちょろちょろしてたのなら、きっとたくさんの: "There's a fair amount of foot traffic here, so if a bunch of little kids were darting around, we must have caused a lot of trouble for a lot of people."
かもしれません。ここは観光区画ではなくて、地元の人たちの生活圏寄りですから。ご近: "Maybe so. This isn't the tourist district, it's closer to where the locals go about their daily lives. We might have been a real nuisance to the neighborhood."
あー……、うん。そういえばさ。幽霊も音楽を聞くのかな: "Ah... yeah. Come to think of it, do ghosts listen to music too?"
智仁がふとそんなことを言ったのだ。俺の隣で。同じように川の流れを見下ろしながら。: Tomohito suddenly said that right next to me, looking down at the flowing river just like I was.
どうしていきなりそんなことを言うんだろうかこいつは。: Why is this guy bringing that up out of nowhere?
いや、わるい。この石橋に関する“噂”をふと、思い出したんだけどさ: "Nah, my bad. I just suddenly remembered the 'rumor' about this stone bridge."
それってどんな“噂”で、どんな“不思議”なのだろう。: What kind of "rumor" and what kind of "mystery" was it?
そう問いかける俺に、智仁が答える前に、: Before Tomohito could answer my question,
あ、幽霊……？ 私もそれ、知ってるよ？: "Ah, ghosts...? I know that one, too!"
えっと、この町には夜とは違うもうひとつ“夜”が、どこかにあって……: "Um, somewhere in this town, there's another 'Night' that's different from the regular night..."
そこから抜け出した幽霊とか、そうじゃないモノとか色々と、昼も夜もなく、そこら辺を: "And ghosts, or things that aren't ghosts, slip out from there and walk around the area day and night. That was the 'rumor,' right? If I remember correctly."
夜とは違うもうひとつの“夜”: Another "Night" that's different from the regular night.
その点については“噂”でも“謎”でも何でもないのだと知っているけれど……。: As far as that part went, I knew it was neither a "rumor" nor a "mystery" at all, though...
幽霊とは違う、色々なモノ: "All sorts of things that are different from ghosts..."
そうだよー。怖いのだったり。やさしいのだったり。かわいい動物みたいなもの、だった: "That's right! Scary ones. Nice ones. Ones that are like cute animals. There are all kinds!"
俺は辺りを何気なく見まわした――どこかに“夜”へと続く抜け穴でもぽっかり空いたま: I casually looked around the area--wondering if a loophole leading to the "Night" was still gaping open somewhere.
帰ってきてすぐの柊先輩が知っていて、ずっとこの町に住んでる先輩が“初耳だなあ”“: "It's kind of funny how Hiiragi-senpai, who just got back, knows all about it, while Senpai, who's lived in this town the whole time, has this look on his face like, 'That's the first I've heard of it, amazing.'"
くすくすと千和が笑う。ほんとにねー、とハルも笑いながら、続けた。: Chiwa giggled. "Right?" Haru laughed along too, and continued.
もしも怖い幽霊に出会ってしまったら。そして捕まってしまったら。どこか遠くへ連れて: "The adults used to tell us that if you met a scary ghost and got caught, you'd be taken away somewhere far off. So they told us to go to sleep early at night."
私もその噂、聞いたことがあります。確かこの橋には幽霊は追ってこれないから……: "I've heard that rumor, too. If I remember right, ghosts can't chase you onto this bridge..."
うんうん。だからもし幽霊に追いかけられたらこの橋を目指して走ろうねって。そんな噂: "Mhm, mhm. So if you ever got chased by a ghost, you were supposed to run for this bridge. I feel like that was the rumor."
はは。まあだいたいさ、噂話とか怪談だとか。そういうのは子どものしつけの代わりだっ: "Haha. Well, usually, rumors and ghost stories like that are just a substitute for disciplining kids, or a way to force stubborn children to behave."
……ああ、うん。なんだか俺も思い出してきたぞ: "...Ah, yeah. I think it's coming back to me, too."
“この橋に幽霊が追ってこれない”……そんな噂を検証しようよ！ って。そんなことを: "'Ghosts can't chase you onto this bridge'... Haru suddenly suggested we test that rumor out! I just remembered how we all gathered here in the middle of the night once."
あれは確か夜中も夜中、深夜過ぎのこと。: If I recall, it was the dead of night, well past midnight.
子どもたちだけで出歩くにはあまりにも遅い時間だった。: It was way too late for a bunch of kids to be out walking around by themselves.
『なあ、ハル。別にこんなこと、わざわざ検証することないって』: "Hey, Haru. We don't really need to go out of our way to test something like this, do we?"
『そ、そうだよお。それもこんな遅い時間に……さむいよ、ねむいよ、ちょっとこわいよ: "T-That's right. Especially this late at night... It's cold, I'm sleepy, and it's a little scary... Achoo!"
『だめだよふたりとも。だめだめだ。何を弱気なこと言ってるの。“謎”はちゃんと調べ: "No way, you two. Absolutely not. Why are you being such wimps? If we don't investigate 'mysteries' properly, they might turn into 'dangers' someday, you know!"
『私たちの内の誰かがもし、怖い幽霊に追いかけられちゃうようなことがあったとして…: "Suppose one of us ever gets chased by a scary ghost... If that happens, we just have to run for this spot. Wouldn't you feel relieved knowing that for sure?"
『ねえ、ハルちゃん。ハルちゃんは幽霊とか信じちゃう人なの？』: "Hey, Haru-chan. Are you the type of person who actually believes in ghosts?"
『うん。もちろんだよ。信じちゃう人だよ、私』: "Yep. Of course I am. I totally believe in them."
『だってこの世界には魔法も魔法少女も小さなちいさな神さまも、そして喋る猫だってい: "Because in this world, there's magic, and magical girls, and tiny, tiny gods, and even talking cats! It wouldn't be fair if there weren't at least a few ghosts too, right?"
『あ～……そうですねえ。ハルちゃんの言いたいこと、少しだけわかる気がします。ほん: "Ah~... Well, that's true. I feel like I kind of understand what Haru-chan is trying to say. Just a tiny bit."
『でもどうやってそれを検証するのかな。このままじっと待つ感じ？ 幽霊が出るまで？: "But how are we supposed to test it? Are we just going to stand here and wait? Until a ghost shows up?"
『うーん。それしかないのかなあ』: "Hmm. I wonder if that's the only way."
『ううん。違う。それじゃあだめだ……こちらから探しに行こうか』: "No. Wait. That won't work... Let's go look for them ourselves."
『だってテレビでよくやってるよね。たくさん幽霊が住んでるはずの有名な心霊スポット: "Because they show it on TV all the time, right? Even at famous haunted spots where tons of ghosts are supposed to live, the second a TV camera shows up, they all get shy and won't come out, right?"
『だからこちらからお出迎えに行くんだね？』: "So we're going to go out and welcome them ourselves?"
『え、ええ～……っ、わざわざ自分から怖いものを見つけに行くんですか？ そ、そんな: "E-Eeeh~...?! We're going out of our way to find something scary on purpose? N-No way, I don't want to. Absolutely not."
『そうだね。確かにちょっと、そういう危なそうなのは……』: "Yeah. Going after something that sounds that dangerous really is a bit..."
『ううん、大丈夫！ 元気があったらきっと幽霊だって逃げてくよ！』: "No, it'll be fine! As long as we stay upbeat, I bet even the ghosts will run away!"
『……探してる相手を逃げさせちゃあだめじゃないか』: "...Wait, isn't it bad if we scare off the very things we're looking for?"
『とにかく行こうよっ、シャイな幽霊さんたちをお迎えに上がりましょー』: "Anyway, let's go! Let's go welcome those shy little ghosts!"
『あ～……だめだ。こうなっちゃもう誰もハルを止められないから……諦めるしかないの: "Ah~... It's no use. Once Haru gets like this, nobody can stop her... We might just have to give in."
拳を振り上げたハル。: Haru thrusting her fist into the air.
どうしても幽霊を怖がり涙目だった千和。: Chiwa with tears in her eyes, utterly terrified of ghosts.
面倒だから早く終わらないかなあお布団恋しいと欠伸を繰り返していた姫織。: Himeori yawning over and over, wishing the hassle would end quickly so she could get back to her beloved futon.
ひとりだけどこか上の空であった、あの頃の智仁。: Back then, Tomohito was the only one with his head in the clouds.
そんなみんなに囲まれて、いつもよりうれしそうに微笑んでいたあず咲先輩。: Surrounded by all of us, Azusaki-senpai was smiling even more happily than usual.
そんな場面をふと思い出せたのだった。: That scene suddenly came back to me.
俺たちの住む参禅町は結構広い。: Sanzen Town, where we live, is pretty big.
それでいて、そこかしこに“うつくしい景色”“楽しい場所”“不思議な一瞬”そういっ: And yet, everywhere you look, it's overflowing with each and every one of those things--"beautiful scenery," "fun places," and "mysterious moments."
一日掛けてもそれらを全部、この瞳に映して歩くことは困難だろう。: Even if we spent a whole day walking around, it would be hard to take all of them in with our own eyes.
在りし日の俺たちはそんなこの町が好きだった。: In days gone by, we loved this town for being like that.
一日中走り回って遊んでも飽きることはなかったし、その度に新しい顔を見せてくれるこ: We never got tired of running around and playing all day long, and as little kids, our hearts must have raced every time the town showed us a new side of itself.
そんな俺たちの町は今、いっぱいの春色に溢れている。: And right now, our town is overflowing with the colors of spring.
“うつくしい景色”のそのひとつを、ここでならぐるりと見渡せた。: From right here, we had a panoramic view of one of those pieces of "beautiful scenery."
山の上の施設だ。その門前付近にある広場。: It was the facility up on the mountain. The plaza near its front gate.
俺たちはベンチに座り各自お弁当を広げていた。: We sat on the benches and unpacked our respective lunches.
俺のお弁当を覗き込んだ姫織が目をキラキラさせていた。: Himeori's eyes sparkled as she peered into my lunchbox.
あさひさんから渡されたのはお重のお弁当箱だった。: What Asahi-san had handed me was a multi-tiered bento box.
だからなんとなく予想というか、想像くらいはできていたのだが……。: Because of that, I had a vague idea of what to expect, or at least I could imagine it, but...
おせち料理みたいに手が込んでるね。どれもおかずがキラキラしてるよ。量もいっぱいで: "It's as elaborate as a New Year's feast. Every single side dish is practically sparkling. And there's so much of it... It must've been really hard to make."
うん。だからたぶん、みんなで分け合って食べなさいってことじゃないかな。あさひさん: "Yeah. So I think this is probably her way of telling us to share it with everyone. That sounds just like something Asahi-san would say."
昨日のお花見で食べたお弁当もあさひさんが用意してくれた。: Asahi-san had also prepared the bento we ate at yesterday's flower viewing.
そのときもまた手の込んだ立派なものだったのだ。: That one had been a magnificent, elaborate spread as well.
いつも本当にありがとうあさひさん。: Thank you so much for everything, Asahi-san.
それぞれがそれぞれのお弁当でお腹を満たし――それでも足りない者は（主に姫織が）俺: Everyone filled their stomachs with their own lunches--and those who still didn't have enough (mainly Himeori) picked at my huge bento--as we took a short break from our treasure hunt.
広場は町を展望するための整備が成されている。: The plaza was set up as an observation deck overlooking the town.
手すり付きの柵。その手前に百円玉で使用できる双眼鏡。いくつかのベンチ。東屋のよう: A fence with a handrail. Coin-operated binoculars right in front of it that took hundred-yen coins. Several benches. A roofed rest area like a gazebo.
小さな公園のようでもあった。: It was almost like a small park.
みんなが思い思いに過ごす中、俺はその様子を少し離れた場所から見つめていた。: While everyone spent their time however they liked, I watched them from a short distance away.
広場はさくらの木々に囲まれている。: The plaza was surrounded by cherry trees.
風が吹けば花びらが晴れ渡る空を流れていった。: Whenever the wind blew, petals drifted across the clear sky.
ふわふわ漂う甘い香りが、胸だけでなく心までをも満たしていくような。: The sweet scent wafting softly through the air felt like it was filling not just my lungs, but my heart as well.
大きなさくらの木を背に腰を下ろして、漂う甘い香りを胸いっぱいに吸い込んでいると、: As I sat down with my back against a large cherry tree, taking a deep breath of that sweet fragrance,
背にした木の背後から、そーっと伸びてくる小さな手に気付く。: I noticed a small hand reaching out ever so slowly from behind the tree I was leaning against.
その手は、腰を下ろした隣に置いておいたお弁当に伸びていた。: That hand was reaching for the bento I had set down next to me.
まだ半分くらい残っている、蓋を開けたままのお弁当だ。: It was still about half full, with the lid left open.

小さく名前を呼んだけど、それに十夜は気づかず……。: I softly called her name, but she didn't notice...

おかえり、ふたりとも。今日は楽しい一日だったかな: "Welcome back, you two. Did you have fun today?"

大雅もお肉でいいかな。今夜のご飯: "Are you fine with meat for dinner tonight too, Taiga?"

ふたりが台所に立つ。: The two of them stood in the kitchen.
何も手伝うことのない俺は居間で待っていることにした。: Having nothing to help with, I decided to wait in the living room.

ブラウン管の古いテレビだ。: It was an old CRT television.
[・|こ][・|こ]は“月と太陽の狭間の時間”だ。“夜”でなければ“昼”でもない: *This place* is the "time between the moon and the sun." It is neither "Night" nor "Day." Because of that, I was curious about what kind of programs would be on.

どうなっているんだろう。これもまた“魔法”だろうか。: How does this even work? Is this "magic" too?

設定された[・|俺][・|た][・|ち]以外の誰にも繋がらない“魔法”の端末だ。: A "magical" device that couldn't connect to anyone other than *us*, the ones it was set up for.
呼び出し音が鳴る。いつまでも。ずっと。: The dial tone rang. On and on. Forever.
残念だが落胆するほどではなかった。: It was a shame, but not enough to make me feel discouraged.

……声が聴きたい。: I want to hear her voice.
[わけ|理由]もなくそう思ってしまったからだ。: I had thought that for no real reason at all.

一応四人分は作ったけど……。今夜は戻って来てくれるかな: "I made enough for four just in case, though... I wonder if she'll come back tonight."
あさひさんが配膳をしてくれながら言った。: Asahi-san said while setting the table.

特に“みんなで一緒に”とか、“みんなで、仲良く”だとか。: Especially things like "all of us together," or "everyone getting along."
[・|そ][・|う][・|い][・|っ][・|た][・|こ][・|と]は行き過ぎ: Because when *things like that* go too far--to the point where the person on the receiving end feels repulsed--it feels like it becomes almost no different from violence.

いただきます。……すごい。美味しそう: "Thank you for the food. ...Wow, this looks delicious."

むしろ楽しいんだよとあさひさんは笑う。私は料理作るの好きだから、と。: In fact, it's fun, Asahi-san laughed, adding that she loves cooking.
大雅や十夜が美味しそうに食べてくれる。そんなふたりを見られるんだなあって想像する: "You and Toya always eat it with such gusto. Just imagining getting to see the two of you like that makes all the hard work disappear completely."
そんなこと言われたら……あさひさん: "When you put it like that... Asahi-san..."

きょとんとした。意外だとばかり。: She blinked in surprise, looking completely caught off guard.

いつもと変わらぬ朝だった。: It was an ordinary morning, no different from usual.
秒針の音に満たされた部屋。: A room filled with the sound of the second hand.
カーテンを閉め忘れていた窓から朝の光が差し込んでいる。: Morning light streamed in through the window where I had forgotten to close the curtains.
どんな日もいつもと変わらず朝が来る。: No matter the day, morning comes just the same as always.
数ある時計のひとつで時刻を確認した。: I checked the time on one of the many clocks.

とても大切な、意味ある夢を見ていたような。: It felt like I had been dreaming of something very important, something meaningful.

いつからだろう、と思う。: Since when has it been like this, I wonder.
いつから夜に見た夢を思い出せなくなったんだろう。: When did I stop being able to remember the dreams I had at night?

秒針の音に溢れる部屋はあまり居心地がいいとは言えず――……: A room overflowing with the sound of ticking second hands couldn't really be called comfortable --...

寝床からもぞもぞ抜けだし支度を調える。: I sluggishly crawled out of bed and got ready.
ネクタイを締める手がまごついている。: My hands fumbled as I tied my necktie.
